sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Winslow?
sections.html:
A Winslow sale needs two separate inspections: a township resale certificate from the Construction Official and a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate from the Winslow Township Fire District. Winslow also differs from its neighbors in size, since it is the largest municipality in Camden County and much of its land sits in the Pinelands.

The sections below cover the market numbers, the two inspections and their fees, the Camden County deed filing and the township tax rules. After that comes a plain comparison of listing, selling by yourself and accepting an as-is cash offer.

sections.h2: How does the Winslow housing market look on paper?
sections.html:
Winslow Township had 39,907 residents at the 2020 census and an estimated 40,562 in mid-2025. It spreads over 57.42 square miles of land, so density is only 695 people per square mile, which fits the pine woods and farm parcels between its villages.

sections.h2: What shaped Winslow's neighborhoods and the Pinelands around them?
sections.html:
Winslow was incorporated on March 8, 1845 from part of Gloucester Township, and its early economy ran on glass works that drew on local timber, clay and sand. By the 1970 census it still had only 11,202 residents.

Growth followed the Atlantic City Expressway interchange at Williamstown Road, finished in 1965. Levitt and Sons then built thousands of homes in the Sicklerville section, and the population reached 20,034 in 1980 and 30,087 in 1990. Today the township includes unincorporated communities such as Sicklerville, Cedar Brook, Blue Anchor, Tansboro, Braddock, Albion and Williamstown.

A large share of the land is protected. Wikipedia reports that about 80 percent of the township lay in the Pinelands National Reserve as of 2006. The New Jersey Pinelands span 1.1 million acres, and the Pinelands Commission can be reached at (609) 894-7300. If your property is a larger lot or a buyer plans a new structure, ask the Commission what approvals apply before you promise anything.

sections.h2: Which roads, buses and schools matter to Winslow buyers?
sections.html:
Winslow has 245.16 miles of roadway, split among the township, Camden County, the state and the South Jersey Transportation Authority. The Atlantic City Expressway crosses the southwest corner with Exits 31, 33, 38 and 41, and U.S. Route 30, Route 73 and Route 143 also cross town.

Transit means buses. NJ Transit's 400 route links Sicklerville with Philadelphia, and the Avandale park-and-ride has 322 parking spaces. Wikipedia notes that no bus stops within reasonable walking distance of the municipal building, so most households drive.

Winslow Township School District has eight schools and 5,024 students in 2023-24. It has four elementary schools for pre-kindergarten to grade 3, two upper elementary schools for grades 4 to 6, a middle school for grades 7 and 8 and Winslow Township High School. The district formed in 1998 after voters approved a split from the Lower Camden County Regional district, and it also teaches students from Chesilhurst.

sections.h2: What resale certificate does Winslow require?
sections.html:
Winslow requires a certificate of continued occupancy, renamed a resale certificate in a February 2025 ordinance, for every existing dwelling before a change in occupancy. The application goes to the Township Construction Official, who inspects whether the unit is fit for habitation and meets the township code.

  • The application fee is $100 for a residential dwelling.
  • Payment by check triggers a 10 working-day wait before the inspection.
  • The Construction Official has 10 working days after a complete application and fee to inspect and issue or list the violations.
  • The first reinspection is free, and each later one costs $50.
  • No one may occupy the dwelling until life-hazard violations are corrected.
  • Violations carry a penalty between $250 and $1,000.

The ordinance has an unusual option: a buyer can take over the seller's duty by signing a written waiver that states the buyer knows they are responsible for the certificate. The waiver must be filed with the Construction Official.

sections.h2: What does the Winslow fire inspection involve?
sections.html:
New Jersey law requires a smoke and carbon monoxide alarm inspection before a home is sold, and in Winslow the Fire Prevention Division does it. A firefighter sprays test smoke into each alarm, presses the carbon monoxide test button and checks any secondary power source label. If everything passes, you get a certificate to bring to settlement.

  • The fee is $65 with eight or more days of notice, $100 with four to seven days and $150 with three days or fewer.
  • A senior aged 62 or older with proof of age pays $30.
  • A reinspection or a missed appointment costs $35 each.
  • Alarms older than ten years must be replaced, and the manufacture date is printed on the underside of the device.
  • A house with solar panels, a generator or battery storage needs a permanent printed label that says multiple sources of power.
  • The fire district will not enter a house on a lockbox, and the office says it responds within 24 hours of an online application.

A house with no fuel-burning appliance, fireplace or attached garage needs only smoke alarms. Call the Fire Marshal at 609-561-4225 with any question about your layout.

sections.h2: Where is the deed recorded, and how do Winslow taxes work?
sections.html:
Winslow is in Camden County, so deeds are recorded by the Camden County Clerk at Room 102, 520 Market Street in Camden, phone (856) 225-5300. The clerk's page lists electronic recording and appointment scheduling, so your title company can usually file for you.

Property taxes are due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. A 10-day grace period applies, but the township must physically hold the payment by the end of the tenth day, since postmarks do not count. Delinquent amounts up to $1,500 carry 8 percent interest and larger ones carry 18 percent, and a balance above $10,000 at year end adds a 6 percent penalty. Anything left in the township drop box counts as received the next business day.

Added and omitted assessment bills go out in October and are due November 1. The 2026 tax sale was held on October 8, and the township notes that taxes, utility charges and other municipal charges are tied to the property itself. Ask the tax office for a payoff figure before closing.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell myself, or take a cash offer in Winslow?
sections.html:
Listing usually brings the widest pool of buyers, a cash offer cuts the two-inspection process, and a sale on your own saves commission if you handle the paperwork well. The right pick turns on the shape of the house and your deadline.

  • List if the house is in good order and you can wait for a mortgage buyer to pass the township inspection.
  • Sell on your own if you will manage showings, the contract and both Winslow inspections.
  • Take an as-is cash offer if repairs, tenants or an estate would slow a conventional sale, since the buyer can sign the resale waiver and take on any violations.

Whichever route you pick, ask the Fire District for an inspection date as soon as you have a closing date, and file the township application early enough to allow the 10 working days the ordinance gives the inspector.

faqs.q: What does a Winslow resale certificate cost?
faqs.a: The township application fee is $100 for a residential dwelling. The first reinspection is free and later ones cost $50. The separate fire inspection costs $65 to $150 depending on notice, with a $30 senior rate.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the Winslow resale certificate, the seller or the buyer?
faqs.a: The seller by default, but a buyer may take it over with a written waiver filed with the Construction Official. The waiver must state that the buyer knows they are assuming responsibility for the certificate.

faqs.q: How long does the Winslow fire inspection take to schedule?
faqs.a: The fire district says it contacts you within 24 hours of an online application, and fees rise when you give less than eight days of notice. The certificate must be in hand at settlement.

faqs.q: When are Winslow property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a 10-day grace period. Postmarks do not count, and interest runs back to the original due date on late payments.

faqs.q: Where are deeds recorded for Winslow houses?
faqs.a: At the Camden County Clerk's office, Room 102, 520 Market Street in Camden. The phone number is (856) 225-5300.
